name: AXT, Inc.
thesis_sentence: AXT is the only Western-listed merchant supplier of indium phosphide substrates at the exact moment InP became the gating raw material for AI datacenter optical transceivers and lasers, and it is tripling capacity into a backlog that already exceeds a full year of historical revenue.
thesis_bullets: InP has flipped from a slow telecom-niche substrate to the constrained input for 800G/1.6T optical engines and emerging co-packaged optics; AXT is a top-three global merchant InP source and the only one outside Japan/China captive supply chains, so the AI optical buildout pulls directly through AXT's furnaces.

The ramp is contracted, not hoped-for: InP backlog crossed $100M in Q1 2026 (up from >$60M one quarter earlier) versus FY2025 total company revenue of only $88M, and management is doubling InP capacity to a $35M/quarter run-rate by end-2026 and guiding to $65-70M/quarter ($260-280M annualized) by end-2027/early-2028.

The April 2026 equity raise (~$632.5M gross, 9.84M shares at $64.25) fully funds the capacity tripling and recapitalizes a previously cash-strapped balance sheet; the company now sits on roughly $700M cash against ~$12M debt, removing the financing overhang that historically capped the multiple.

catalysts.title: InP backlog crossed $100M, a full year of legacy revenue under contract
catalysts.body: AXT's indium phosphide backlog exceeded $100M in Q1 2026, up from more than $60M in Q4 2025. For context, total company revenue was $88.3M for all of FY2025. The backlog is concentrated in AI datacenter optical customers buying InP wafers for transceiver lasers and photodetectors. This is the cleanest forward-demand signal in the substrate space and the single most important driver of the re-rating.

catalysts.title: Capacity doubling to $35M/quarter InP by end-2026
catalysts.body: Management is doubling InP capacity in 2026 to a $35M/quarter run-rate (~$140M annualized for InP alone) by repurposing existing Tongmei facilities rather than greenfield, keeping incremental capex efficient. InP already accounted for over 50% of Q1 2026 revenue. Hitting the $35M/quarter exit rate would roughly double trailing total revenue on the InP line alone.

catalysts.title: Second capacity doubling to $65-70M/quarter by end-2027/early-2028
catalysts.body: Beyond the 2026 doubling, AXT guides to a further doubling of InP capacity to $65-70M/quarter ($260-280M annualized) by end-2027 or early 2028. Management frames scale-out optical orders as roughly doubling in 2026 and again in 2027, with a potential co-packaged-optics (CPO) demand inflection in 2028-2029 layered on top. This is a multi-year revenue CAGR well above 50%.

catalysts.title: Gross margin inflecting on InP mix
catalysts.body: Non-GAAP gross margin jumped to 29.9% in Q1 2026 from 21.5% in Q4 2025, driven by volume and a favorable mix shift toward higher-value InP. AXT's historical gross margin sat in the mid-teens to low-20s on a commodity GaAs/Ge base. As InP scales past 50-60% of revenue, structural gross margin should migrate toward the 35%+ range, with operating leverage on a largely fixed Tongmei cost base.

catalysts.title: Recapitalized balance sheet removes the financing overhang
catalysts.body: The April 2026 underwritten offering raised ~$632.5M gross (9,844,357 shares at $64.25 including the fully-exercised over-allotment). Combined with the $128.4M cash position at year-end 2025, AXT now holds roughly $700M cash against only ~$12M debt. The capacity tripling is fully funded without further dilution, and the balance-sheet risk that historically suppressed the multiple is gone.

catalysts.title: Scarcity value: the only Western merchant InP at scale
catalysts.body: InP substrate supply is dominated by Japanese captive/IDM sources (Sumitomo, JX) and Chinese players. AXT, via its Tongmei subsidiary, is the largest merchant InP supplier accessible to Western fabless optical and laser customers seeking supply diversification away from single-country concentration. As hyperscalers and optical module makers qualify second sources, AXT is the default beneficiary of the diversification mandate.

catalysts.title: China export permits now flowing for InP
catalysts.body: After China added InP to its export-control list in February 2025, AXT secured the permits needed to resume shipments; Q3 2025 revenue beat guidance once licenses were granted. While permits add ~3 months of lead time, the permitting regime is functioning, and the friction arguably deepens AXT's moat by raising the barrier for new entrants and reinforcing customers' need to lock in qualified supply early via backlog.

catalysts.title: Tongmei STAR Market IPO as a value-crystallization event
catalysts.body: AXT's vertically integrated China subsidiary Tongmei has a planned listing on Shanghai's STAR Market. A successful IPO would mark Tongmei's standalone value (raw material processing, crystal growth, recycling, all in-house) at a China-tech multiple, potentially well above the value embedded in AXT's consolidated US market cap, and provide local growth capital. The 7.28% redeemable noncontrolling interest is currently carried at ~$49M.

catalysts.title: Vertical integration on critical raw materials
catalysts.body: Tongmei is vertically integrated across gallium, indium and germanium raw-material processing, crystal growth, furnace fabrication and recycling on a single China campus. This insulates AXT from the very raw-material export controls that disrupt competitors and gives it cost and supply-security advantages as the same critical minerals (gallium, germanium) face Chinese export restrictions imposed since August 2023.

catalysts.title: Optical-sector tailwind and analyst target upgrades
catalysts.body: The AI optical complex (Coherent, Lumentum, Applied Optoelectronics) has re-rated violently higher in 2026 on 800G/1.6T transceiver demand, and AXT sits upstream of all of them as the substrate supplier. Sell-side targets have been ratcheting up: Northland to $125 (Outperform) and Wedbush to $80 from $28 (Outperform), reflecting rapidly rising forward revenue estimates as the capacity ramp de-risks.

business_facts.what_it_does: AXT designs and manufactures high-performance compound and single-element semiconductor substrates: indium phosphide (InP), gallium arsenide (GaAs), and germanium (Ge) wafers. These substrates are the base material on which optical, RF, LED, photonic and solar devices are built. Manufacturing is concentrated in China through its majority-owned subsidiary Tongmei.
business_facts.segments: Reported by substrate material: InP (>50% of Q1 2026 revenue, the AI-optical growth driver), GaAs (RF, photonics, LED), Ge (solar, optics), plus consolidated raw-material/recycling joint ventures.

peers_positive_read: AXT is the upstream substrate supplier to the entire AI-optical complex (Coherent, Lumentum, Applied Optoelectronics, Fabrinet, POET). Those names have re-rated to extreme multiples on 800G/1.6T transceiver demand; AXT supplies the InP wafers underneath them and trades on the same secular driver one layer up the stack, with arguably better scarcity characteristics because merchant InP supply is so concentrated.

valuation_lens.method: EV/Sales on a forward revenue ramp
valuation_lens.read: On the bull ramp (InP exiting 2027 at ~$260-280M annualized, total company approaching $390M+ in FY2028), today's ~$5.9B EV is ~15x FY2028 sales, falling toward 10x as the second doubling lands. For the fastest-growing, capacity-tripling name in a complex where peers trade at 10-40x forward sales, the bull argues the multiple is defensible if execution holds and gross margin structurally clears 35%.
